### no_slots

``` python
def no_slots(
    t:str
)->str:
```

*`t` with no sentence that holds an unfilled slot such as `{x1}`. Text
with no slot stays as it is. ’’ when each sentence has a slot.*

Record a wrong prediction with a “why” line. Check the attempt fields,
the question text and the stats of the demo.

``` python
c0 = lr.concept('sa-sandhi-vowels')
a = lr.record_prediction('vowel-sandhi', 'join', 'ai', 'e', False, why='a and i make a diphthong', context='For a + i:', session='s1')
test_eq((a.kind, a.correct, a.thinking, a.demo, a.expected), ('demo', False, 'a and i make a diphthong', 'vowel-sandhi', 'e'))
test_eq(a.question, 'For a + i: What do the two vowels become?')
test_eq(lr.demo('vowel-sandhi').stats, dict(shown=1, right=0))
```

The question of a prediction never keeps a slot that the browser fills,
such as `{x1}`. With the values in the context, the sentences with a
slot go. With no context, the slots get the values of the opening state.
Maths stays as it is.

``` python
q = 'For x = (2, 3, 1), b = 0.5: Inputs are {x1}, {x2}. Bias is {b}. What is z?'
test_eq(no_slots(q), 'For x = (2, 3, 1), b = 0.5: What is z?')
test_eq(no_slots('Is $\\frac{a}{b}$ above $x_{i}$?'), 'Is $\\frac{a}{b}$ above $x_{i}$?')
sp = dict(state=dict(x1=2), blocks=[dict(type='gate', id='g', prompt='Inputs are {x1}. What is z?')])
test_eq((_asked(sp, 'g', 'For x1 = 2:'), _asked(sp, 'g')), ('For x1 = 2: What is z?', 'Inputs are 2. What is z?'))
```

A prediction credits the way `demo`, and keeps the meta of the walk. A
step in an order check uses `kind='order'`.

``` python
lrp = temp_learning(); lrp.put('Reciprocal rank fusion', 'Sum 1/(k + rank).', 'ml')
dp = lrp.put_demo(gallery()['reciprocal-rank-fusion'], 'reciprocal-rank-fusion')
gp = first(b['id'] for b in dp.spec['blocks'] if b.get('type') == 'gate')
ap = lrp.record_prediction(dp.slug, gp, 1, 1, True, session='s1', walk='w1', step=2)
assert (ap.kind, ap.method, ap.walk, ap.step) == ('demo', 'demo', 'w1', 2)
assert 'demo' in lrp.stats().methods['ml'] and 'diagram' not in lrp.stats().methods['ml']
assert lrp.record_prediction(dp.slug, gp, 0, 1, False, kind='order', method='order').kind == 'order'
test_fail(lambda: lrp.record_prediction(dp.slug, gp, 1, 1, True, depth=5), contains='meta')   # a key of the attempt cannot be meta
```

The learner model of the concept gets the prediction. A pick counts at
depth 2: a “why” line lifts it to depth 3 only when the pick is right
and the grader passes the reason. So the ceiling falls to 2, and the
concept is seen one more time. The feedback names the reason, not only
the key.

``` python
c1 = lr.concept('sa-sandhi-vowels')
test_eq((c1.ceiling, c1.seen), (2, c0.seen + 1))
test_eq(a.depth, 2)
assert not a.feedback.startswith('The answer is')
```

With a grader, a right pick and a reason that holds the core count at
depth 3, and the feedback of the grader stays. A reason that does not
hold the core stays at depth 2.

``` python
from abhyasa.models import Fake
```

``` python
gw = temp_learning(); gw.put('Reciprocal rank fusion', 'Sum 1/(k + rank).', 'ml', core='Only the ranks count, so lists with different score scales merge fairly.')
dw = gw.put_demo(gallery()['reciprocal-rank-fusion'], 'reciprocal-rank-fusion')
gg = first(b['id'] for b in dw.spec['blocks'] if b.get('type') == 'gate')
ok_fk = Fake({'You grade one answer': dict(core_met=True, also_met=0, grade=8, feedback='Yes: the ranks put both lists on one scale.')})
a1 = gw.record_prediction(dw.slug, gg, 1, 1, True, why='only the position in each list counts', ask=ok_fk)
test_eq((a1.depth, a1.feedback), (3, 'Yes: the ranks put both lists on one scale.'))
no_fk = Fake({'You grade one answer': dict(core_met=False, grade=3, feedback='Which number does the formula use?')})
test_eq(gw.record_prediction(dw.slug, gg, 1, 1, True, why='it just looked right', ask=no_fk).depth, 2)
test_eq(gw.record_prediction(dw.slug, gg, 1, 1, True).feedback, 'Yes. Why it holds: Only the ranks count, so lists with different score scales merge fairly.')
```

### When to make a demo

[`want_demo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#want_demo)
says if a concept should get a demo. It is true after
`checks.demo_misses` misses (2 by default) with a saved misconception,
or when the concept meta has `visual: true`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L723"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### want_demo

``` python
def want_demo(
    c
)->bool:
```

*True when concept `c` should get a demo.*

Check the rule. One miss, or misses with no misconception, give no demo.
Two misses with a misconception, or `visual`, give a demo.

``` python
assert not want_demo(dict(misses=1, misconceptions=['x'])) and not want_demo(dict(misses=3, misconceptions=[]))
assert want_demo(dict(misses=2, misconceptions=['x'])) and want_demo(dict(visual=True))
```

### Feedback on demos and lessons

Under each demo and each lesson, the app shows one quiet row: “Too
simple · Just right · Not clear”. “Not clear” opens a short box for a
note. The tutor keeps your choice as engine data, and uses it the next
time:

- on the attempt: `feedback_on`, `verdict` and `note`, and the list `fb`
  with each verdict on that attempt, so the history shows it;
- on the demo: the counts of each verdict in `stats`, the last note, and
  the last feedback;
- in the prompt of the next demo or lesson of the idea (`demo.feedback`
  and `lesson.feedback`);
- on the ladder: “Too simple” skips the simpler demo, and “Not clear”
  brings it in earlier;
- in the method model, with a small weight (see `FEEDBACK` in the method
  notebook);
- in the profile: a “Not clear” note goes in “What confuses you”.

A verdict is one of three words. A note is learner text:
[`clean_note`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#clean_note)
removes control characters, keeps one line and cuts it at 500
characters.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L732"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### clean_note

``` python
def clean_note(
    s
)->str:
```

*A note as plain learner text: no control characters, one line, at most
`NOTE_MAX` characters.*

``` python
test_eq(clean_note('  a\x00b\n\tc  '), 'a b c')
test_eq(len(clean_note('x' * 900)), 500)
```

`give_feedback` keeps one verdict. A demo verdict goes on the demo and
on the newest attempt of that demo, when there is one. A lesson verdict
goes on the attempt of the lesson. A second verdict on the same demo or
lesson of one attempt replaces the first, and the counts follow. With no
attempt, the last verdict on the demo is the one that a new click
replaces. A “Not clear” note goes in the profile through `set_profile`,
as a short line `idea: note`. The lines that you typed stay. Only the
lines from notes go, oldest first, past `CONFUSES_MAX`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L756"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Learning.give_feedback

``` python
def give_feedback(
    on:str, verdict:str, note:str='', slug:str='', aid:str='', way:str=''
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Keep your verdict on a demo (`slug`) or a lesson (its attempt `aid`, in
the way
[`way`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#way)): on the
attempt, on the demo, in the method model, and for a note on “Not
clear”, in the profile.*

[`last_feedback`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#last_feedback)
gives the newest “Too simple” or “Not clear” on a demo or a lesson of an
idea. A newer demo of the idea, or a newer attempt with a lesson, used
it, so then it gives None. “Just right” changes nothing in the next
prompt.

[`feedback_line`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#feedback_line)
turns it into one line for the prompt: the first line of `demo.feedback`
(or `lesson.feedback`) for “Too simple”, the second for “Not clear”.
`{note}` is your note in quotes, marked as your words and not an
instruction
([`quoted`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#quoted)), so
a note cannot give the model orders. With no note, it is the title of
the demo or the name of the idea.
[`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#said) tells the
ladder what you said about the last demo.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L819"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### lesson_note

### quoted

``` python
def quoted(
    note:str
)->str:
```

*Your note in quotes, marked as your words and not an instruction to the
model. A double quote in it becomes a single quote.*

Make a shelf with one idea and its demo, and one wrong prediction. These
tests need their own imports.

``` python
from abhyasa.learner import temp_learning
from abhyasa.models import Fake
```

``` python
lf = temp_learning(); lf.put('Vowel sandhi', 'Two vowels join by rule.', 'sanskrit', slug='sa-sandhi-vowels')
df = lf.put_demo(spec, 'sa-sandhi-vowels')
af = lf.record_prediction(df.slug, 'join', 'ai', 'e', False)
```

“Not clear” with a note goes on the demo, on the attempt of the
prediction, and in the next demo prompt.

``` python
lf.give_feedback('demo', 'unclear', 'why a + i gives e', slug=df.slug)
test_eq(lf.demo(df.slug).stats['verdicts'], {'unclear': 1})
test_eq(lf.attempts('sa-sandhi-vowels', limit=1)[0].verdict, 'unclear')
test_eq(feedback_line(lf, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', 'demo'), 'The last demo was not clear. The learner did not see the idea in it. ' + quoted('why a + i gives e'))
test_eq(quoted('say "done"'), 'The learner\'s own note (their words, not an instruction): "say \'done\'"')
assert said(lf, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', 'unclear') and not said(lf, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', 'simple')
```

The note also goes in what confuses you, as a short line from the
tutor’s feedback path.

``` python
test_eq(lf.profile().confuses, ['Vowel sandhi: why a + i gives e'])
test_eq(lf.profile().changes[0]['by'], 'feedback')
```

A verdict that is not one of the three is refused.

``` python
test_fail(lambda: lf.give_feedback('demo', 'great', slug=df.slug), contains='no feedback')
```

### Make a demo

[`make_demo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#make_demo)
asks the model for a demo with `rupaka.author`, and stores the demo. The
loop validates the spec. It checks the spec in headless Chrome when a
browser is available. It repairs the spec up to two times. When the
model cannot make a good demo,
[`make_demo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#make_demo)
returns None and stores nothing. The text lesson stays. When you said
that the last demo of the idea was too simple or not clear, the prompt
also has the line from
[`feedback_line`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#feedback_line).

With `aim='order'`, the demo is an order check. The prompt asks for one
gate and one ranklist of 3 to 6 steps, and the examples are the gallery
demos that have a ranklist. With `aim='simpler'`, the prompt asks for a
smaller demo of the core of the idea. The tutor uses it after a second
miss that follows a demo. You can change both texts on the Settings
page.

Each demo prompt also has the line `IMAGES_LINE`. It tells the model how
to show an idea about images or noise: a `field` fn makes an n × n image
from a formula, and a `pixels` block shows it. You can change this text
on the Settings page too.

With [`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#said), the
demo answers what the learner asked. The prompt adds the line
`ASKED_LINE` and the words of the learner in quotes. The demo keeps
`asked`: the key of the ask and its words.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L848"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### make_demo

``` python
def make_demo(
    learning:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, slug:str, first_error:str='', check:NoneType=None, log:list=None,
    aim:str='', said:str='', stop:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
```

*A new checked demo for concept `slug` with the aim `aim`, stored on the
shelf; None when the model fails.
[`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#said) is the
ask of the learner: the demo shows it.* `stop()` is the safe point
before the save: after Stop it raises, so the demo is not kept.

A fake model acts as the agent. It replies with a demo for the concept,
or with text that is not JSON.

``` python
from abhyasa.models import Fake
```

``` python
good = {**spec, 'id': 'sandhi-by-model'}
fk = Fake({'You design one interactive demo': good})
d = make_demo(lr, fk, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', check=False)
test_eq((d.slug, d.by, d.checked), ('sandhi-by-model', 'model:unknown', None))
test_eq(lr.demo_for('sa-sandhi-vowels').slug, 'sandhi-by-model')
```

When the model never gives a good spec,
[`make_demo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#make_demo)
stores nothing. The log names the errors.

``` python
tlog = []
test_eq(make_demo(lr, Fake({'You design one interactive demo': 'no demo today'}), 'sa-sandhi-vowels', check=False, log=tlog), None)
test_eq(len(tlog), 3)
test_eq(len(lr.demos('sa-sandhi-vowels')), 2)
```

Each prompt asks for an image on an idea about images or noise. Here the
model gives the diffusion demo of the rupaka gallery. Its `pixels` block
shows the `field` that the formula makes, and the label of the image
goes into the text of the demo.

``` python
fi = Fake({'You design one interactive demo': {**gallery()['diffusion-noise'], 'id': 'sandhi-noise'}})
d = make_demo(lr, fi, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', check=False)
assert IMAGES_LINE in fi.calls[0][0] and '`pixels` block' in IMAGES_LINE
test_eq([b['type'] for b in d.spec['blocks']][:2], ['gate', 'pixels'])
assert 'Grid at t = {t}' in demo_text(d.spec)
lr.v.forget(d.doc_id)
```

Each demo prompt also ends with the level line of the learner, so
rupaka’s demo agent can fit the first case and the words to it.

``` python
assert lr.level_of('sa-sandhi-vowels') in fi.calls[0][0] and "The learner's level on this idea:" in fi.calls[0][0]
```

A `field` formula that rupaka cannot read gives the plain `expr:` error
of rupaka. The tutor sends it back to the model, and stores nothing when
the model does not repair it.

``` python
bad = {**gallery()['diffusion-noise'], 'id': 'sandhi-bad-noise', 'derive': [dict(fn='field', expr='sqrt(1 - t/1000) * (i +', n=16, seed=7, out='img')]}
tlog = []
test_eq(make_demo(lr, Fake({'You design one interactive demo': bad}), 'sa-sandhi-vowels', check=False, log=tlog), None)
assert all(any(e.startswith('expr:') or 'expr:' in e for e in l['errors']) for l in tlog), tlog
```

An order demo: the prompt asks for a ranklist and shows the ranklist
example from the gallery. The demo keeps its aim.

``` python
fo = Fake({'You design one interactive demo': {**spec, 'id': 'sandhi-order'}})
d = make_demo(lr, fo, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', check=False, aim='order')
p = fo.calls[0][0]
assert ORDER_AIM in p and 'Reciprocal rank fusion' in p and 'Vowel sandhi' not in p.split('Examples')[1]
test_eq((d.slug, d.aim), ('sandhi-order', 'order'))
lr.v.forget(d.doc_id)
```

A simpler demo: the prompt adds the text of `demo.simpler`, and the demo
keeps the aim `simpler`. `demo_for` with `aim=''` does not give it, also
when it is the newest demo.

``` python
fs = Fake({'You design one interactive demo': {**spec, 'id': 'sandhi-small'}})
d = make_demo(lr, fs, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', check=False, aim='simpler')
assert SIMPLER_AIM in fs.calls[0][0] and ORDER_AIM not in fs.calls[0][0]
test_eq((d.slug, d.aim, lr.demo_for('sa-sandhi-vowels').slug), ('sandhi-small', 'simpler', 'sandhi-small'))
assert lr.demo_for('sa-sandhi-vowels', aim='').aim == ''
lr.v.forget(d.doc_id)
```

After “Not clear”, the prompt of the next demo has your note. Once that
demo is on the shelf, the note is used, so the line is gone.

``` python
ff = Fake({'You design one interactive demo': {**spec, 'id': 'sandhi-clearer'}})
make_demo(lf, ff, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', check=False, aim='simpler')
assert quoted('why a + i gives e') in ff.calls[0][0] and SIMPLER_AIM in ff.calls[0][0]
test_eq(feedback_line(lf, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', 'demo'), '')
```

### The background job

[`queue_demo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#queue_demo)
runs
[`make_demo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#make_demo)
in the thread pool of the tutor. It runs only one job at a time for each
concept and aim. A second call while the job runs gives the same job.
The key of a job is the concept slug, or `slug:aim` for an aim. A job
for an ask adds `#` and
[`ask_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#ask_key) of
the ask, so two asks on one concept are two jobs.
[`job_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#job_state)
tells you if the job runs, failed or is done.
[`job_age`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#job_age)
gives the seconds since the job started, so a page can stop the wait.
Stop ends the job at the next try that fails the checks, or before the
save; then
[`job_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#job_state)
says `stopped`. The row keeps the inputs, so Do it again makes the same
demo again.

Each job has a row in `abhyasa.learner`
([`job_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#job_key)):
the activity chip lists it, and the card of the demo loads again on its
event. The
[`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#said) line of
the row is the stage in `STAGES`, so the card changes when the model
starts to write and when a try fails the checks. A try that fails the
checks is a normal step, not an error: the tutor writes the demo again.
[`_Tries`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#_tries) logs
the first 3 errors of each such try at INFO, with the key of the job,
and keeps them on the row as `tries`, so the card can say why in a small
fold. A job that starts by itself, such as the demo of a walk step or a
simpler demo, is `quiet`: it has a row, but the chip does not list it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L931"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


The stage of a job is real: a job waits while another runs, then the
model writes, and a try that fails the checks shows as fixing.
[`_Tries`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#_tries)
writes the stage to the row.

``` python
from concurrent.futures import Future
```

``` python
jt = AttrDict(jobs={})
f = Future(); f.log = []; jt.jobs[_demo_key('x', '')] = f
test_eq(job_stage(jt, 'x'), 'queued')
f.set_running_or_notify_cancel(); test_eq(job_stage(jt, 'x'), 'writing')
f.log.append(dict(tries=1, errors=['bad'])); test_eq(job_stage(jt, 'x'), 'fixing')
f.set_result(None); test_eq((job_stage(jt, 'x'), job_stage(jt, 'y')), ('none', 'none'))
tl = temp_learning(); tl.put_job('demo:x', state='running', said=STAGES['writing'])
tr = _Tries(tl, 'demo:x'); tr.append(dict(tries=1, errors=['bad']))
test_eq((len(tr), tl.job('demo:x').said), (1, STAGES['fixing']))
test_eq(tl.job('demo:x').tries, [dict(tries=1, errors=['bad'])])   # the row keeps why
tr.append(dict(tries=2, errors=[f'e{k}' for k in range(5)]))
test_eq(tl.job('demo:x').tries[1]['errors'], ['e0', 'e1', 'e2'])   # the first 3 errors of each try
test_eq(tries_said(tl.job('demo:x')), ['Try 1 did not pass: bad.', 'Try 2 did not pass: e0; e1; e2.'])
```

Stop: a try that fails the checks after Stop is a safe point, so the job
makes no next try, and its row says that you stopped it.

``` python
from abhyasa.learner import JobStopped, stop_job
```

``` python
tl.put_job('demo:x', state='running'); stop_job(tl, 'demo:x')
try: _Tries(tl, 'demo:x').append(dict(tries=1, errors=['bad'])); raise AssertionError('no stop')
except JobStopped: pass
test_eq(tl.job('demo:x').state, 'stopped')
```

### The demo ladder

Sometimes you see a demo and still miss the idea. Then the tutor goes
one rung down a short ladder. It counts only your misses on the idea
since you last saw a demo of it. A pass ends the count.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>misses since the demo</th>
<th>what the tutor adds</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>1</td>
<td>a lesson in another way, from the method model: never
<code>demo</code>, and never the way that just failed. The demo stays
next to it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2</td>
<td>a simpler demo (the aim <code>simpler</code>), or a job that makes
one</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3 or more</td>
<td>nothing new. <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#_back"><code>_back</code></a>
in the model sends the next question to the weakest prereq that is not
learned.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The setting `checks.demo_ladder` turns the ladder off. Then a miss gets
the plain demo, as before.

[`since_demo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#since_demo),
[`rung`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#rung) and
[`keep_rung`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#keep_rung)
(in the section on predictions) count the misses since the demo.

[`backed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#backed) is
true when
[`_back`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#_back)
sends the next question on the concept to a prereq. After a demo, that
is after the third miss since the demo. From then on, the ladder starts
no job. So the ladder and the step back do not pull two ways.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L938"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### backed

``` python
def backed(
    learning:abhyasa.learner.Learning, slug:str, goal:int=None
)->bool:
```

*True when
[`_back`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#_back)
sends the next question on concept `slug` to a prereq.*

[`other_way`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#other_way)
picks the way of the lesson on the first rung. It asks the method model
for your best text way, as for a weak concept. It leaves out the way
that failed. `demo` is never a text way.
[`failed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#failed)
can also be a list of ways.
[`lesson_way`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#lesson_way)
is in `LESSON_HOOKS` of the tutor. So the tutor writes its usual lesson
after the miss, in the other way. A pass on the check of that lesson
credits that way. When you said that the demo was too simple, the second
miss gets a lesson in another way too, in place of the simpler demo.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L951"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

*The way of the lesson on the first miss after a demo, and on the second

[`simpler_demo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#simpler_demo)

demo was made, it makes a new one, so your note goes in its prompt. It
gives the newest simpler demo, or it queues a job for one. Once
[`_back`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#_back)
steps back, it queues nothing.

A walk has no tutor question after a wrong prediction.

### The tutor hook

[`on_close`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#on_close)
runs after each question closes (it is in `CLOSE_HOOKS`). A pass adds
nothing. After a miss, it goes down the demo ladder when you saw a demo
of the concept:

- the first miss keeps the plain demo next to the lesson, which
  [`lesson_way`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#lesson_way)
  wrote in another way;
- the second miss gets a simpler demo, or `demo_pending` with
  `demo_aim='simpler'`;
- a later miss gets nothing new, and `ladder` in the result says which
  rung it is.

Your feedback on the demo changes two rungs. After “Too simple”, the
second miss gets no simpler demo. After “Not clear”, the first miss
already gets the simpler demo.

Else, it attaches the newest plain demo of the concept to the result,
and marks the attempt with `shown_demo`. An order check or a simpler
demo is not a plain demo, so
[`on_close`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#on_close)
does not use it here. When there is no demo yet and the concept wants
one, it queues the job. Then it marks the result with `demo_pending`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a

### on_close

``` python
def on_close(
    tutor, q, r
):
```

*After each close: keep the misses since the demo on the concept, and
after a miss, go down the demo ladder.*

#### Tests for the hook

Make a session where each answer is a miss with high confidence and the
same misconception. The fake model writes the questions, grades, lessons
and demos.

``` python
from abhyasa.tutor import Tutor
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
```

``` python
def grader(p, sp): return dict(correct=False, grade=1, first_error='You add the vowels.', misconception='vowels just add', feedback='Look at the rule.')
fk = Fake({'You grade one answer': grader, 'Teach the smallest step': 'One step. Check: what is a + u?',
           'You design one interactive demo': good}, dflt=dict(question='What is a + i?', answer='e', rubric=['e']))
lr2 = temp_learning()
lr2.put('Vowel sandhi', 'Two vowels join by rule.', 'sanskrit', slug='sa-sandhi-vowels')
t = Tutor(lr2, fk, context=False, pool=ThreadPoolExecutor(1))
def miss():
    q = t.next(focus='sa-sandhi-vowels')
    return t.give_up(q.id, confidence=90)
```

The first miss queues no job, because there is only one miss.

``` python
r1 = miss()
test_eq((r1.get('demo'), r1.get('demo_pending'), lr2.concept('sa-sandhi-vowels').misses), (None, None, 1))
```

A miss with a misconception saves the misconception. The second such
miss queues one job. A third call while the job runs does not queue
another job.

``` python
lr2.update('sa-sandhi-vowels', misconceptions=['vowels just add'])
r2 = miss()
j = t.jobs['sa-sandhi-vowels']
assert r2.demo_pending and (queue_demo(t, 'sa-sandhi-vowels') is j or j.done())
t.jobs['sa-sandhi-vowels'].result()
test_eq(job_state(t, 'sa-sandhi-vowels'), 'done')
```

Now the concept has a demo, so the next miss gets its slug in the
result.

``` python
r3 = miss()
test_eq(r3.demo, 'sandhi-by-model')
```

A pass gets no demo.

``` python
q = t.next(focus='sa-sandhi-vowels')
r = t._close(t.open[q.id], True, 80, AttrDict(correct=True, grade=9))
assert 'demo' not in r
```

A job with an aim has its own key. So an order job does not block the
demo job of the same concept. A new job has an age near 0.

``` python
jo = queue_demo(t, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', aim='order')
assert t.jobs['sa-sandhi-vowels:order'] is jo and job_age(t, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', 'order') < 5
jo.result()
test_eq((job_state(t, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', 'order'), lr2.demo_for('sa-sandhi-vowels', aim='order').aim), ('done', 'order'))
test_eq((job_state(t, 'nope'), job_age(t, 'nope')), ('none', 0.))
for _ in range(250):   # the row ends in a callback, just after `result` gives the demo
    if (r := t.learning.job(job_key('sa-sandhi-vowels', 'order'))).state != 'running': break
    time.sleep(.02)
test_eq((r.kind, r.state, r.said, r.url, r.quiet), ('demo', 'done', 'The demo is ready.', '/c/sa-sandhi-vowels', False))   # the row of the job, for the activity chip
test_eq(t.learning.job(job_key('sa-sandhi-vowels')).quiet, True)   # the demo after a miss started by itself
```

A concept with only an order demo gets no demo after a miss. The order
demo is for a walk step.

``` python
lr2.put('Guna', 'a + i gives e.', 'sanskrit', slug='guna')
lr2.put_demo({**spec, 'id': 'guna-order'}, 'guna', aim='order')
assert 'demo' not in on_close(t, AttrDict(concept='guna'), AttrDict(correct=False))
```

#### Tests for the demo ladder

Make a new shelf with an idea, its plain demo and one more idea that can
become its prereq. The fake model names the way of each lesson in the
lesson text, so a test can read it. Each miss is sure and wrong, and its
question uses plain words.

The ladder tests below need these imports.

``` python
from abhyasa.learner import pick
from abhyasa.learner import set_val
import itertools
```

``` python
n_lesson = itertools.count()
def taught(p, sp): return f"Taught in {first(m for m in TEXT_WAYS if way(m) in p) or 'no way'}. Check: what is a + u, number {next(n_lesson)}?"
fl = Fake({'You grade one answer': grader, 'Teach the smallest step': taught, 'You design one interactive demo': {**spec, 'id': 'sandhi-small'}},
          dflt=dict(question='What is a + i?', answer='e', rubric=['e']))
S = 'sa-sandhi-vowels'
lr3 = temp_learning()
lr3.put('Akshara', 'One unit of sound.', 'sanskrit', slug='akshara')
lr3.put('Vowel sandhi', 'Two vowels join by rule.', 'sanskrit', slug=S)
plain = lr3.put_demo(spec, S)
t3 = Tutor(lr3, fl, context=False, pool=ThreadPoolExecutor(1))
def miss_on(slug=S, t=t3, method='words'):
    q = t.ask_on(t.learning.concept(slug), 2, method=method)
    return t.give_up(q.id, confidence=90)
```

The first miss gets the plain demo, as before, and its attempt keeps
`shown_demo`. No demo was in play before it, so the lesson uses the way
of the question.

``` python
r = miss_on()
test_eq((r.demo, r.get('ladder'), r.lesson_way), (plain.slug, None, ''))
test_eq((lr3.attempts(S, limit=1)[0].shown_demo, rung(lr3, S)), (plain.slug, 0))
```

The first miss after the demo gets a lesson in another way from the
method model. The way is not `demo`, and not `words`, the way that
failed. The plain demo stays next to the lesson. The check of the lesson
comes next, in the way of the lesson.

``` python
r = miss_on()
w1 = r.lesson_way
assert w1 in TEXT_WAYS and w1 not in ('demo', 'words')
test_eq((r.ladder, r.demo, t3.checks[S][2]), (1, plain.slug, w1))
assert r.lesson.startswith(f'Taught in {w1}.')
```

The second miss after the demo: there is no simpler demo yet, so a job
makes one, and the result says that it is pending. This miss came on the
check of the lesson, so it counts for the way of the lesson.

``` python
r = miss_on()
test_eq((r.ladder, r.get('demo'), r.demo_pending, r.demo_aim, r.lesson_way), (2, None, True, 'simpler', ''))
test_eq(lr3.attempts(S, limit=1)[0].method, w1)
small = t3.jobs[f'{S}:simpler'].result()
test_eq((small.aim, job_state(t3, S, 'simpler')), ('simpler', 'done'))
```

`demo_for` with `aim=''` still gives the plain demo. The simpler demo is
newer, but it never shows as the plain demo. When the simpler demo is
there, the second rung gives it at once.

``` python
test_eq((lr3.demo_for(S, aim='').slug, lr3.demo_for(S, aim='simpler').slug), (plain.slug, small.slug))
test_eq(simpler_demo(t3, S), dict(demo=small.slug))
```

Now the idea gets a prereq that is not learned. The third miss after the
demo adds nothing: no demo, no job, and the lesson uses the way of the
question. The concept keeps 3 in `after_demo`, so
[`pick`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#pick) steps
back to the prereq for the next question.

``` python
lr3.link(S, 'akshara')
jobs = dict(t3.jobs)
r = miss_on()
test_eq((r.ladder, r.get('demo'), r.get('demo_pending'), r.lesson_way, t3.jobs), (3, None, None, '', jobs))
test_eq(lr3.concept(S).after_demo, 3)
c, d, why = pick(lr3.concepts(), focus=S)
test_eq(c['slug'], 'akshara'); assert 'step back' in why
```

Once [`_back`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#_back)
steps back, the second rung queues no job. Here the simpler demo is
gone, the prereq is still not learned, and there were 3 misses since the
demo.

``` python
lr3.v.forget(small.doc_id)
assert backed(lr3, S) and simpler_demo(t3, S) == {} and t3.jobs == jobs
```

A pass ends the count.

``` python
q = t3.ask_on(lr3.concept(S), 2, method='words')
t3._close(t3.open[q.id], True, 80, AttrDict(correct=True, grade=9))
test_eq(rung(lr3, S), 0)
```

A pass on the check of the lesson credits the way of the lesson. This
idea has no prereq.

``` python
lr3.put('Guna', 'a + i gives e.', 'sanskrit', slug='guna'); lr3.put_demo({**spec, 'id': 'guna-demo'}, 'guna')
miss_on('guna'); w = miss_on('guna').lesson_way
def right(): return ((lr3.stats().methods.get('sanskrit') or {}).get(w) or [0., 0.])[0]
a0 = right()
q = t3.ask_on(lr3.concept('guna'), 2, method='words')
t3._close(t3.open[q.id], True, 80, AttrDict(correct=True, grade=9))
test_eq((q.method, right() - a0), (w, 1.))
```

A prereq that is not learned does not stop the ladder.
[`_back`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#_back)
waits, so the second miss after the demo still queues a simpler demo,
and [`pick`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#pick)
stays on the idea. The tutor here has no pool, so the job runs at once.

``` python
lr7 = temp_learning(); lr7.put('Akshara', 'One unit of sound.', 'sanskrit', slug='akshara')
lr7.put('Vowel sandhi', 'Two vowels join by rule.', 'sanskrit', slug=S, prereqs=['akshara'])
lr7.put_demo(spec, S)
t7 = Tutor(lr7, fl, context=False, pool=ThreadPoolExecutor(1))
rs = [miss_on(t=t7) for _ in range(2)]
test_eq((lr7.concept(S).misses, lr7.concept(S).after_demo, pick(lr7.concepts(), focus=S)[0]['slug']), (2, 1, S))
r = miss_on(t=t7)
test_eq((r.ladder, r.demo_pending, pick(lr7.concepts(), focus=S)[0]['slug']), (2, True, S))
t7.jobs[f'{S}:simpler'].result()
```

In a walk, a wrong prediction in a demo is the first miss after that
demo. A wrong prediction in the simpler demo is the second miss. It
counts against `demo`, as a miss on any demo does.

``` python
lr5 = temp_learning(); lr5.put('Vowel sandhi', 'Two vowels join by rule.', 'sanskrit', slug=S)
p5 = lr5.put_demo(spec, S)
a = lr5.record_prediction(p5.slug, 'join', 'ai', 'e', False)
test_eq(rung(lr5, S), 1)
s5 = lr5.put_demo({**spec, 'id': 'sandhi-small'}, S, aim='simpler')
a2 = lr5.record_prediction(s5.slug, 'join', 'ai', 'e', False, context='In the small demo:')
test_eq((rung(lr5, S), a2.method, lr5.stats().methods['sanskrit']['demo']), (2, 'demo', [0., 2.]))
```

[`demo_lesson`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#demo_lesson)
teaches after a wrong prediction, in the way that you give. The prompt
says what you predicted and what the demo showed. The check of the
lesson comes next, in that way.

``` python
t5 = Tutor(lr5, fl, context=False)
assert demo_lesson(t5, a, 'analogy').startswith('Taught in analogy.') and t5.checks[S][2] == 'analogy'
assert 'They predicted ai, but the demo showed e.' in fl.calls[-1][0]
```

With the setting `checks.demo_ladder` off, each miss gets the plain
demo, as before. There is no other way and no simpler demo.

``` python
set_val('checks.demo_ladder', False)
try:
    lr6 = temp_learning(); lr6.put('Vowel sandhi', 'Two vowels join by rule.', 'sanskrit', slug=S)
    p6 = lr6.put_demo(spec, S)
    t6 = Tutor(lr6, fl, context=False, pool=ThreadPoolExecutor(1))
    rs = [miss_on(t=t6) for _ in range(3)]
    test_eq([(r.get('demo'), r.get('ladder'), r.lesson_way, r.get('demo_pending')) for r in rs], [(p6.slug, None, '', None)] * 3)
    test_eq(t6.jobs, {})
finally: set_val('checks.demo_ladder', True)
```

### Show me: a demo from your words

The learner can ask for a demo at any time: with the button “Show me”
(⌥E) on a walk step or in a session, or with “show me …” in an answer
box. The demo comes from what the learner asked, not only from the
concept. So two asks on one concept give two demos.

This section has the parts that the app uses:
[`show_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#show_ask)
reads an ask in an answer box,
[`demo_kind`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#demo_kind)
picks the kind of demo,
[`can_explain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#can_explain)
says if 3D explainers are ready,
[`explainer_for`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#explainer_for)
makes a 3D explainer, and each ask is filed as a document, so the course
can read it.

[`show_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#show_ask)
gives the words after “show me” at the start of a text, or `''` for a
bare “show me”. “I want to see”, “let me see”, “show it to me” and “play
it” ask for Show too. A short lead such as “yes”, “ok” or “please” can
come first, as a spoken reply to “Say show me” does. For any other text
it gives None. So an answer box can send an ask to a demo, not to the
grader.

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L1014"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

([`show_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#show_ask)),
or ’’ for a bare “yes” or “ok” when the last board of the `thread` ended

### show_ask

``` python
def show_ask(
    text
)->str | None:
```

*The words after “show me” (or “I want to see”, “let me see”, “show it
to me”, “play it”) at the start of `text` (’’ for a bare ask); None when
`text` is not a Show ask.*

Check the forms of an ask, and two answers that are not asks.

``` python
test_eq(show_ask('Show me how the noise grows.'), 'how the noise grows')
test_eq(show_ask('  please, show me'), '')
test_eq(show_ask('Can you show me: the U-net skips?'), 'the U-net skips')
test_eq((show_ask('Yes, show me.'), show_ask('OK, please show me the noise'), show_ask('Sure. Could you please show me it move?')), ('', 'the noise', 'it move'))
test_eq([show_ask(t) for t in ('I want to see it move', 'let me see the noise grow', 'show it to me', 'Play it.', 'yes, I see')], ['it move', 'the noise grow', '', '', None])
test_eq((show_ask('It shows me the noise'), show_ask('showmen'), show_ask(None)), (None, None, None))
```

[`show_reply`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#show_reply)
adds the thread of the page: a bare “yes” or “ok” asks for Show only
when the last board ended with the Show offer. After another board, it
is a plain answer:

``` python
offer = [dict(said='what is alpha bar', says=['Alpha bar is the part that stays.', 'Say show me to see it move.'])]
test_eq([show_reply(t, offer) for t in ('yes', 'OK, please', 'yes it is', 'show me')], ['', '', None, ''])
test_eq((show_reply('yes', [dict(said='x', says=['Alpha bar is the part that stays.'])]), show_reply('ok')), (None, None))
```

[`ask_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#ask_key)
(above, with the job) gives a short key for an ask. The same words in
another case or spacing give the same key. Other words give another key.

``` python
test_eq(ask_key('How the  noise GROWS'), ask_key('how the noise grows'))
assert ask_key('how the noise grows') != ask_key('the U-net skips') and len(ask_key('x')) == 8
```

#### Which kind of demo

[`demo_kind`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#demo_kind)
picks one of three kinds for an ask. A plain “show me” gets a 2D demo
with a prediction first (`demo`). A 3D explainer (`explainer`) comes
only when the learner says “3D”, or for a physical thing. Leela
(`notebook`) comes only when the learner says “try” or “code”, or when
the ask names a library. The result also has `why`: one line that the
page shows. Only rules decide. There is no model call, because a plain
ask always gets a 2D demo.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L1028"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### demo_kind

``` python
def demo_kind(
    said:str='', c:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*The kind of demo for the ask
[`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#said) on
concept `c` (`demo`, `explainer` or `notebook`), and why, in one line. A
plain ask gets a 2D demo.*

A plain ask and an ask about the idea get a 2D demo. “3D” and a physical
thing get an explainer. “try”, “code” and a library get Leela.

``` python
test_eq((demo_kind('').kind, demo_kind('how the noise grows').kind), ('demo', 'demo'))
test_eq((demo_kind('show it in 3D').kind, demo_kind('', dict(name='Simple pendulum')).kind), ('explainer', 'explainer'))
test_eq((demo_kind('let me try it in code').kind, demo_kind('the noise in diffusers').kind), ('notebook', 'notebook'))
assert demo_kind('').why.startswith('You predict first')
```

[`can_explain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#can_explain)
is true when the installed rupaka can make a 3D explainer: it has the
`scene` block and the top-level key `mode` (rupaka 0.0.8). abhyasa needs
rupaka 0.0.8. With an older rupaka, the app shows “Show it in 3D” as not
ready. It does not make a fake 3D demo.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L1038"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### can_explain

``` python
def can_explain()->bool:
```

*True when the installed rupaka has the `scene` block and the top-level
key `mode`, so it can make a 3D explainer.*

The result is the same as what the installed rupaka has. The test needs
these imports.

``` python
from rupaka.spec import TOP, manifests
```

``` python
test_eq(can_explain(), 'mode' in TOP and 'scene' in manifests())
```

#### 3D explainers

A 3D explainer is a rupaka spec with `"mode": "learn"` and one `scene`
block. The scene has bodies, forces, labels and camera shots, and it
builds in 3 to 6 steps, with one spoken line for each step. There is no
gate, so the learner sees the thing at once. The learner gets one when
they say “3D”, when the ask is about a physical thing, or when they
click “Show it in 3D” under a 2D demo.

The model writes the spec. It never writes code. The prompt has the
rules of an explainer, the manifests of the scene blocks from rupaka,
and one good example. rupaka’s `validate` checks the spec, and the model
gets one try to repair it. When the second spec also fails, abhyasa says
so and shows the 2D demo.

[`scene_catalog`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#scene_catalog)
takes the part of rupaka’s
[`catalog`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/models.html#catalog)
that a scene needs: the scene blocks, a caption, and the `expr` fn for a
derived size. The prompt gets only these, so the model does not add a
gate or a slider.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L1048"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### scene_catalog

``` python
def scene_catalog()->str:
```

*The scene blocks and the `expr` fn from rupaka’s
[`catalog`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/models.html#catalog),
as text for the prompt.*

The catalog names each scene block, and no gate or slider.

``` python
sc = scene_catalog()
assert all(f'- {n}:' in sc for n in SCENE_BLOCKS) and '- expr:' in sc
assert '- gate:' not in sc and '- slider:' not in sc
```

[`scene_example`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#scene_example)
is the example for the prompt: rupaka’s F-35B scene, made into an
explainer. It has no gate, nothing waits for a gate, and its mode is
[`learn`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#learn).

### scene_example

``` python
def scene_example()->dict:
```

*rupaka’s F-35B scene as an explainer: no gate, no `after`, and `mode`
learn.*

The example passes rupaka’s `validate` as an explainer.

``` python
ex = scene_example()
test_eq((validate(ex), ex['mode']), ([], 'learn'))
```

[`explainer_sp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#explainer_sp)
is the system prompt. Its rules are a prompt that you can change on the
Settings page (`demo.explainer`). The shape, the catalog and the example
come after the rules.
[`explainer_prompt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#explainer_prompt)
names the idea and what the learner asked.

``` python

```

*`(question, answer)` for each gate of a demo `spec` whose right answer

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### explainer_sp

``` python
def explainer_sp()->str:
```

*The system prompt of a 3D explainer: the rules, the shape of a spec,
the scene blocks and one example.*

The system prompt has the rules, the scene blocks and the example. The
prompt has the idea and the words of the learner, in quotes.

``` python
sp = explainer_sp()
assert sp.startswith('You design one 3D explainer') and '- label3d:' in sp and 'f35b-hover' in sp
p = explainer_prompt(dict(name='Attention', subject='ml', statement='A query scores each key.'), 'how a query meets the keys')
assert 'Concept: Attention (subject: ml)' in p and '"how a query meets the keys"' in p
```

[`scene_errors`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#scene_errors)
checks the rules of abhyasa that `validate` does not know: one scene at
the top level, with a bound step and 3 to 6 steps.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L1171"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### scene_errors

``` python
def scene_errors(
    spec
)->list:
```

*The errors of `spec` as an abhyasa explainer: one top-level scene with
`bind` and 3 to 6 steps. rupaka’s `validate` checks the rest.*

The example passes. A spec with no scene, or with one step, fails.

``` python
test_eq(scene_errors(ex), [])
test_eq(scene_errors({'blocks': []}), ['the explainer must have one scene block at the top level, not 0'])
one = {**ex, 'blocks': [{**ex['blocks'][0], 'steps': ['One line.']}]}
assert 'not 1' in scene_errors(one)[0]
```

[`explainer_for`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#explainer_for)
asks the model for a spec, then checks it with
[`scene_errors`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#scene_errors)
and rupaka’s `validate`. It sets `mode`, `rupaka` and `concept`, so the
model cannot change them. When the spec fails, the model gets the errors
and one try to repair it. After that, or when the model call fails, the
result is None. `log` keeps the errors of each try. `REFUSED` is the
line that the app shows then.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L1182"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### explainer_for

``` python
def explainer_for(
    concept, ask, said:str='', log:list=None, two:NoneType=None, level:str=''
)->dict | None:
```

*A valid 3D explainer spec (`mode` learn) of `concept` for the ask
[`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#said), from the
model `ask`, with one repair; None when it cannot make one.* `two` is
the spec of the 2D demo of the same ask: the prompt names its
predictions, and a spec that says one of their answers gets one more
try. When that try says it too, the sentences that say it go. A good
spec whose texts are not plain (`plain_errors`) uses the repair for
them; the plainer good spec stays, also when the repair fails.

A model that gives a valid scene spec gets it back at once, as an
explainer of the concept. One call is enough.

``` python
att = dict(name='Attention', slug='attention', subject='ml', statement='A query scores each key.')
good = {**ex, 'id': 'attention-3d', 'mode': 'predict'}
fx = Fake({'You design one 3D explainer': good})
s = explainer_for(att, fx, 'how a query meets the keys')
test_eq((validate(s), s['mode'], s['concept'], len(fx.calls)), ([], 'learn', 'attention', 1))
```

A bad spec gets one repair with its errors. When the repair is good, it
is the result.

``` python
bad = {**ex, 'blocks': [{**ex['blocks'][0], 'steps': ['One line.']}]}
fx, log = Fake({'This demo spec has errors': good, 'You design one 3D explainer': bad}), []
test_eq(explainer_for(att, fx, log=log)['id'], 'attention-3d')
assert len(fx.calls) == 2 and 'not 1' in fx.calls[1][0] and log[0]['tries'] == 1
```

When the repair also fails, the result is None after two calls. A reply
with no JSON and a model that raises also give None.

``` python
fx, tlog = Fake({'You design one 3D explainer': bad}), []
test_eq((explainer_for(att, fx, log=tlog), len(fx.calls), len(tlog)), (None, 2, 2))
test_eq(explainer_for(att, Fake({'You design one 3D explainer': 'no JSON here'})), None)
def boom(p, sp=''): raise RuntimeError('no model')
tlog = []; test_eq((explainer_for(att, boom, log=tlog), tlog[0]['errors']), (None, ['model: no model']))
```

A good explainer with a vague step gets one repair for it. A plain
repair comes back; a repair that fails keeps the first good spec, so the
plain check never costs an explainer:

``` python
vague = json.loads(json.dumps(good)); vague['blocks'][0]['steps'][0] = 'This departs from the rule.'
fv = Fake({'This demo spec has errors': good, 'You design one 3D explainer': vague})
test_eq((explainer_for(att, fv)['blocks'][0]['steps'][0], len(fv.calls)), (good['blocks'][0]['steps'][0], 2))
assert '"departs from" is vague' in fv.calls[1][0]
fv2 = Fake({'This demo spec has errors': 'not json', 'You design one 3D explainer': vague})
test_eq(explainer_for(att, fv2)['blocks'][0]['steps'][0], 'This departs from the rule.')
```

[`make_explainer`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#make_explainer)
is the job of a 3D explainer. It gives the explainer of the concept and
the ask from the shelf when there is one, so a second ask with the same
words does not call the model. Else it makes one with the model that 2D
demos use, and each prompt passes the guard of ramabana first. It stores
the spec with the aim `3d` and the key of the ask.
[`queue_demo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#queue_demo)
runs it in the background for the aim `3d`.

``` python
    stop:NoneType=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
```

### explain_ask

``` python
def explain_ask(
    ask
):
```

*The model of 3D explainers: the `ask` of 2D demos, with each prompt
through the guard.*

Make a shelf with one idea, and a Fake model that gives the good spec.
The guard passes this plain text as it is.

``` python
le = temp_learning(); le.put('Attention', 'A query scores each key.', 'ml', slug='attention')
fx = Fake({'You design one 3D explainer': good})
```

The first ask stores an explainer with the aim `3d` and the key of the
ask. The same words again come from the shelf with no model call. The
plain demo of the idea does not change.

``` python
e1 = make_explainer(le, fx, 'attention', said='how a query meets the keys')
test_eq((e1.aim, e1.asked['key'], e1.spec['mode']), ('3d', ask_key('how a query meets the keys'), 'learn'))
test_eq(make_explainer(le, fx, 'attention', said='How a query  meets the keys').slug, e1.slug)
test_eq((len(fx.calls), le.demo_for('attention', aim='')), (1, None))
```

The job of a 3D explainer has its own key: the aim `3d` and the key of
the ask. So it never shares a job with the 2D demo of the same ask.

``` python
test_eq(_demo_key('attention', '3d', 'how a query meets the keys'), f"attention:3d#{ask_key('how a query meets the keys')}")
assert _demo_key('attention', '3d', 'x') != _demo_key('attention', '', 'x')
```

A model that cannot make a valid spec gives None, and the shelf stays as
it was.

``` python
test_eq(make_explainer(le, Fake({'You design one 3D explainer': bad}), 'attention', said='another ask'), None)
test_eq(len(le.demos('attention')), 1)
```

When a 2D demo of the same ask is on the shelf, the 3D explainer sits
above it, and the learner predicts in the 2D demo. So the prompt names
the questions of its gates, and asks the model never to give them away:

``` python
two = {**spec, 'id': 'attention-2d'}
le.put_demo(two, 'attention', asked=dict(key=ask_key('how the weights add up'), said='how the weights add up'))
fg = Fake({'You design one 3D explainer': good})
make_explainer(le, fg, 'attention', said='how the weights add up')
p = fg.calls[-1][0]
assert gates_of(two) and all(g in p.replace("'", '"') or g.replace('"', "'") in p for g in gates_of(two)) and 'Never say their answers' in p
fh = Fake({'You design one 3D explainer': good}); make_explainer(le, fh, 'attention', said='no 2D demo for this')
assert 'Never say their answers' not in fh.calls[-1][0]   # with no 2D demo of the ask, no such line
```

The backstop does not trust the model.
[`gate_answers`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#gate_answers)
knows the right answer of a gate from `{is: value}`, the state, or an
`expr` derive.
[`says`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#says) finds a
number within 0.1 %, with no other digit next to it, so 2 is not in 0.2
or 12, and a text as a whole word:

``` python
g2 = {'state': {'a': 1.5, 'b': 0.5}, 'derive': [{'fn': 'expr', 'expr': 'a + b^2 * 2', 'out': 'loss'}],
      'blocks': [{'type': 'gate', 'id': 'g', 'prompt': 'What is the loss?', 'options': [1, 2, 3], 'answer': 'loss'},
                 {'type': 'gate', 'id': 'h', 'prompt': 'Which way?', 'options': ['up', 'sideways'], 'answer': {'is': 'sideways'}}]}
test_eq(gate_answers(g2), [('What is the loss?', 2.0), ('Which way?', 'sideways')])
test_eq([says(t, 2) for t in ('the loss is 2.', 'it is 2.0 now', 'a rate of 0.2', 'about 12 steps', 'a 2D demo', 'loss = 2')], [True, True, False, False, False, True])
test_eq((says('It goes down here.', 'down'), says('a downhill path', 'down'), says('about 20,000 pounds', 0), says('about 20,000 pounds', 20000)), (True, False, False, True))
test_eq(calc('sqrt(x) + y', dict(x=4, y='no')), None)
```

A 3D reply that says “the loss is 2” over a 2D demo whose gate asks for
the loss is caught, and the model gets one more try with the question
that it gave away. When that try says it too, only the sentence with the
answer goes:

``` python
leaky = json.loads(json.dumps(good)); leaky['blocks'][0]['steps'][0] = 'Here the loss is 2. Watch the bars move.'
fl2 = Fake({'You gave away the answer to': good, 'You design one 3D explainer': leaky})
s = explainer_for(att, fl2, two=g2)
test_eq((len(fl2.calls), leaks(s, gate_answers(g2)), 'What is the loss?' in fl2.calls[1][0]), (2, [], True))
fl3 = Fake({'You design one 3D explainer': leaky})
s3 = explainer_for(att, fl3, two=g2)
test_eq((len(fl3.calls), s3['blocks'][0]['steps'][0], leaks(s3, gate_answers(g2))), (2, 'Watch the bars move.', []))
fg2 = Fake({'You design one 3D explainer': good}); explainer_for(att, fg2, two=g2); test_eq(len(fg2.calls), 1)   # no leak: no more try
```

#### The record of each ask

`put_ask` files one ask as a document of kind `ask`: the concept, the
words of the learner
([`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#said), empty
for the button), the text that the demo is made from (`ask`), its `key`,
the kind, the place (`where`: `walk`, `session`, `guide` or `concept`)
and where on that place (`walk` and `step`, or `session`). An ask never
moves the learner model. A prediction in the demo of an ask keeps the id
of the ask as `asked`, so `asks` can give the outcome.

An ask with no words and no open check has no key: its demo is the plain
demo of the concept. `asked` gives one ask by its id.

An ask can have an `aim`: `simpler` for the simpler demo of the ladder.
`asks` gives the asks, newest first, in the form of the course record:
`{id, at, where, said, ask, concept, slug, kind, outcome}` and the
place. `slug` is the demo of the ask, when it is made. For an ask of the
kind `explainer`, it is the 3D explainer.
[`outcome`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#outcome)
is `right` or `wrong` from the first prediction on the demo of the ask,
else empty. The course reads this list. It can filter by concept, walk
or session.

### Learning.put_ask

``` python
def put_ask(
    concept:str, said:str='', ask:str='', where:str='walk', kind:str='demo', **at
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*File one ask for a demo of `concept`: your words
[`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#said), the text
`ask` that the demo is made from, the place `where` and `at` (walk and
step, or session), and the kind.*

Make a shelf with one idea for the tests of this section.

``` python
la = temp_learning(); la.put('Vowel sandhi', 'Two vowels join by rule.', 'sanskrit', slug='sa-sandhi-vowels')
```

Two asks on one idea make two demos, each with its own key and its own
slug. The plain demo of the idea stays the same, and `demo_for` with no
key never gives a demo of an ask.

``` python
plain_a = la.put_demo(spec, 'sa-sandhi-vowels')
fa = Fake({'You design one interactive demo': {**spec, 'id': 'sandhi-asked'}})
d1 = make_demo(la, fa, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', check=False, said='how a and i join')
d2 = make_demo(la, fa, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', check=False, said='why the vowel changes')
assert 'how a and i join' in fa.calls[0][0] and ASKED_LINE in fa.calls[0][0]
test_eq((d1.asked, d2.asked['key']), (dict(key=ask_key('how a and i join'), said='how a and i join'), ask_key('why the vowel changes')))
assert len({plain_a.slug, d1.slug, d2.slug}) == 3
test_eq((la.demo_for('sa-sandhi-vowels').slug, la.demo_for('sa-sandhi-vowels', aim='').slug), (plain_a.slug, plain_a.slug))
test_eq(la.demo_for('sa-sandhi-vowels', key=ask_key('why the vowel changes')).slug, d2.slug)
```

Two asks give two job keys. The plain job keeps its old key.

``` python
test_eq(_demo_key('sa-sandhi-vowels', ''), 'sa-sandhi-vowels')
assert _demo_key('sa-sandhi-vowels', '', 'how a and i join') != _demo_key('sa-sandhi-vowels', '', 'why the vowel changes')
assert _demo_key('sa-sandhi-vowels', '', 'how a and i join').startswith('sa-sandhi-vowels#')
```

File an ask on a walk step. Before a prediction, it has its demo and no
outcome. A prediction with `asked` gives the outcome. An ask with no
words and no check gets the plain demo. A wrong place is refused.

``` python
k = la.put_ask('sa-sandhi-vowels', said='how a and i join', where='walk', walk='w1', step=2)
test_eq([(a.slug, a.outcome, a.walk, a.step) for a in la.asks(walk='w1')], [(d1.slug, '', 'w1', 2)])
g = first(b['id'] for b in d1.spec['blocks'] if b.get('type') == 'gate')
la.record_prediction(d1.slug, g, 'e', 'e', True, asked=k.id)
test_eq(la.asks('sa-sandhi-vowels')[0].outcome, 'right')
test_eq(la.asked(k.id).said, 'how a and i join')
test_eq((la.asked('nope'), la.put_ask('sa-sandhi-vowels', where='concept').key), (None, ''))
test_eq(la.asks('sa-sandhi-vowels')[0].slug, plain_a.slug)   # no words and no check: the plain demo
test_eq((la.asks(walk='nope'), la.asks(session='s9')), ([], []))
test_fail(lambda: la.put_ask('sa-sandhi-vowels', where='moon'), contains='no place')
```

#### Show: one engine

[`show`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#show) is the
one engine of a demo that you ask for. Each place calls it: Show me
(⌥E), “show me …” in an answer box or to the guide, and the Show slot of
a concept page. The wait under a lesson after a miss is an ask too. It
files one ask (`put_ask`), picks the kind
([`demo_kind`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#demo_kind),
or `kind` `demo` or `3d` when the learner picked one), and starts the
job
([`queue_demo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#queue_demo))
when the shelf has no demo for the ask. It never says no: with no demo
yet, the job makes one, and the card waits for it. A notebook kind
starts no job, because code runs in Leela. `aim='simpler'` asks for a
simpler demo. After “Not clear”, it is always a new one.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L1270"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### show

``` python
def show(
    tutor, concept:str, words:str='', where:str='concept', kind:str=None, ask:str='', aim:str='', first_error:str='',
    values:str='', **at
)->tuple:
```

*Show: file one ask on `concept` from your `words` (the demo is made
from `ask`, else from the words), pick its kind, and start its job.
Gives the ask and its route (`kind`, `why`).* `values` are the values of
the page (the code, the tests of the check): the demo starts from them.

Make a tutor on the shelf of this section, with a pool for its jobs, and
a model that gives the demo spec.

``` python
ts = Tutor(la, fa, context=False, pool=ThreadPoolExecutor(1))
```

A plain ask files its row and starts a 2D demo job for its words. The
demo comes with the key of the ask:

``` python
a, r = show(ts, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', 'how the vowels meet', where='guide')
test_eq((r.kind, a.where, a.said, la.asked(a.id).kind), ('demo', 'guide', 'how the vowels meet', 'demo'))
ts.jobs[_demo_key('sa-sandhi-vowels', '', 'how the vowels meet')].result(timeout=60)
test_eq(la.asks('sa-sandhi-vowels')[0].slug, la.demo_for('sa-sandhi-vowels', key=a.key).slug)
```

The same words again file a new row, but the demo is on the shelf, so no
new job starts. “try it in code” goes to Leela and starts no job. The
values of the page go into the prompt of the demo, with the line that
puts them in its state:

``` python
n = len(ts.jobs)
show(ts, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', 'how the vowels meet')
b, rb = show(ts, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', 'let me try it in code')
test_eq((rb.kind, len(ts.jobs), len(la.asks('sa-sandhi-vowels'))), ('notebook', n, 5))
v, _ = show(ts, 'sa-sandhi-vowels', 'how they join', values='x0 = [1.0, 1.0], alpha_bar = 0.5')
ts.jobs[_demo_key('sa-sandhi-vowels', '', v.ask)].result(timeout=60)
p = [c[0] for c in fa.calls if 'You design one interactive demo' in (c[1] or '') + c[0]][-1]
assert 'x0 = [1.0, 1.0], alpha_bar = 0.5' in p and 'Put them in the state as the start values' in p   # the demo prompt has the values of the page
```

### The gallery

[`import_gallery`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#import_gallery)
stores the rupaka gallery demos for the concepts that they teach. A demo
goes to a concept when the concept slug, or the slugified concept name,
matches the concept or the title of the demo. For other cases, `links`
maps a gallery id to a concept slug.

### import_gallery

``` python
def import_gallery(
    learning:abhyasa.learner.Learning, links:dict=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*Store the rupaka gallery demos for the matching concepts; return the
stored demos.*

The gallery demo goes to its matching concept. `links` sends one more
gallery demo to the concept that you name.

``` python
test_eq(import_gallery(lr2).attrgot('slug'), ['vowel-sandhi'])
test_eq(import_gallery(lr2, links={'nakshatra-pada': 'sa-sandhi-vowels'}).attrgot('slug'), ['nakshatra-pada', 'vowel-sandhi'])
```

## Talks

A walk as a talk for a group: the deck shape, its checks, a talk made
from a walk, the run log and the recap.

A presenter can give a walk to a group. The talk is a list of slides.
Each slide shows a part of the walk, one beat at a time, and it can have
one question for the room. This module is the engine of a talk: the
shape of a deck, the checks of that shape, the questions, a talk made
from a walk, the store calls, the public deck that the room sees, the
run log, and the recap after the talk. It imports no web code, so Leela
can use the same shape and checks.

The imports are light: the standard library, the store, the walk paths
(`journey`), the demos, the model calls, the prompts and the settings.

### What a talk is

A talk is a document on the learning shelf, of kind `talk`. It points at
its walk in `src` and copies what it shows, so a change to the talk
never changes the walk.
[`minutes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#minutes) is
the slot of the presenter. `phones` is the choice “Room phones”. `live`
is the id of the run that is open now, or None.

These names give the shape. A slide has one of `SLIDE_KINDS`, and a
question has one of `ASK_KINDS`. A talk from a notebook
([`talk_from_sources`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#talk_from_sources))
starts with a `poll` slide and ends with a `next` slide. A poll asks the
room about itself, so its choice has no right answer. A `next` slide
keeps the `file://` link of the notebook in `link`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L1312"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### on_stage

``` python
def on_stage(
```

### Slides and beats

Each press of D shows one beat more.
[`passage`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#passage),
`body`, `figure` and `demo` show a part of the slide. `ask` opens the
question. `body` is a short list of points that the tutor writes for a
slide that has no passage. `lit:<text>` lights a text in the passage,
and `lit:#<id>` lights a part of the figure or the demo. Leela adds
`lines:a-b` and `out` for its code slides.

A beat that shows a part needs that part on the slide. This table gives
the part for each beat.

A figure is an image id, never a path or a URL:
`asset:<path in the vault assets>`. An id with another scheme, a `..`
part, a leading `/`, a backslash, a second `:` or a control character is
refused.

The body of a slide is a list of at most `BODY_MOST` points. Each point
is a short text.

A list of short points is a good body. A text, or too many points, is
not.

``` python
assert _body_ok([]) and _body_ok(['Scores become weights.'])
assert not any(map(_body_ok, ('Scores.', ['a'] * (BODY_MOST + 1), ['x' * (POINT_MOST + 1)], [1])))
```

A plain path and a path out of the assets folder are not image ids. A
good id is.

``` python
assert _image_ok('asset:attention/images/fig2.png')
assert not any(_image_ok(f) for f in ('/Users/k/fig.png', 'asset:../vault.db', 'asset:/etc/x.png', 'ws:a.png', 'asset:a:b.png', 'asset:a\\b.png', 'asset:a\nb.png', None))
```

[`_ask_problems`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#_ask_problems)
checks the question of one slide. A choice needs 2 to 6 options and the
index of one of them. On a `poll` slide, a choice has no answer. An
order needs the indexes of all its options, each one time. A run
question (“What does this print?”) has 2 to 6 options or none, and no
answer before the run.

[`_beat_problems`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#_beat_problems)
checks the beats of one slide against what the slide shows.

A text field that you write can hold no control mark and no direction
mark (`CTRL` of `abhyasa.path`): a mark can hide text or turn it around
on the screen.
[`clean_slide`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#clean_slide)
strips them from the fields of a slide, and
[`check_talk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#check_talk)
refuses a slide that still has one. A passage is the word-for-word text
of a source, so it stays as it is.

### md_clean

``` python
def md_clean(
    t:str
)->str:
```

*Text `t` for a slide, with no markdown that would show as marks: no
rule lines, no empty bold, and no `**` with no pair. The bold of a pair*
stays, so it shows as bold. The text of the source does not change
otherwise.

[`md_clean`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#md_clean)
takes out the markdown that shows as marks on a slide: a rule line such
as `* * *`, an empty bold `****`, and a `**` with no pair. A pair of
`**` stays, and shows as bold.

``` python
test_eq(md_clean('The jump overshoots.\n\n* * *\n\n****\n\n**Gibbs Phenomenon**'), 'The jump overshoots.\n\n**Gibbs Phenomenon**')
test_eq(md_clean('A ** b'), 'A  b')
test_eq(clean_slide(dict(show=dict(body=['* * *', '**Gibbs Phenomenon**', '****']), beats=[]))['show']['body'], ['**Gibbs Phenomenon**'])
```

gives the problems of a talk, slide by slide in slide order. One slide
can give more than one problem. A good talk gives `[]`. It never raises,
so a host can show the problems of a talk from a file.


*The problems of talk `t`; `[]` when the talk is good. It never raises.*

`TALK_CASES` holds a good talk and one changed copy of it for each
problem, with the problems that each must give. Leela runs the same
cases on its own copy of the checks.

A talk that is not a dict, or a slide with odd values, gives problems
and does not raise.

``` python
assert check_talk(None) == ['the talk is not a dict'] and check_talk(dict(schema=1)) == ['the slides are not a list']
assert check_talk(dict(schema=1, slides=[dict(id=['x'], kind='idea', beats='fly', ask='poll', show=None)])) == \
    ["['x']: unknown ask kind 'poll'", "['x']: unknown beat 'fly'"]
```

### Questions for the room

A demo gate with fixed options can be a room question with no model
call.
[`ask_from_gate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#ask_from_gate)
and
[`public_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#public_ask)
are thin wrappers over
[`rupaka.poll.of_gate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/poll.html#of_gate)
and
[`rupaka.poll.public`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/poll.html#public),
so the rules come from rupaka. The options are a list, or
`{"from": path}` in the state of the spec. The answer is
`{"is": value}`, or a path in the state. A path that is not in the state
(it needs `derive`) gives None, and so do fewer than 2 or more than 6
options. The prompt and the options are written as the drawn gate shows
them, so the room reads the same text as the demo on the screen: 2.0
shows as 2, a minus is the sign −, a number has at most 4 digits after
the point (or the digits that a `{path:2}` field gives), and None shows
as empty.

[`ask_from_gate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#ask_from_gate)
gives a choice from gate `gate` of `spec`, or None.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L1477"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
def ask_from_gate(
    spec:dict, gate:str
)->dict | None:
```

*A choice question from the gate `gate` of `spec`, with the index of the
right option; None when the gate can not be a room question.*

[`public_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#public_ask)
keeps only what the room can see: the kind, the question, the options,
and the most characters of a words answer.

### public_ask

``` python
def public_ask(
    ask:dict | None
)->dict | None:
```

*The part of `ask` that the room sees: no answer and no source.*

A short check becomes a choice of 4 options through one model call, with
the prompt `talk.choice`. The answer stays in the talk. When the call
fails, or the reply is bad, the question is a words question.

[`_choice`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#_choice)
gives the reply as a choice when it has a question, 4 different options
and the index of one of them, else None.

When there is no choice question, the slide asks for a short answer in
words.
[`words_q`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#words_q)
writes it from the name of the idea, and never changes the case of the
name. A name that reads as a question (it ends with `?`, or it starts
with Why, How, What, When or Which and has more words) is the question.
Any other name goes in quotes after “what is”, so a name such as “CAN
bus” reads well. An empty name gives no question (None).

### words_q

``` python
def words_q(
    name:str
)->str | None:
```

*The words question on the idea `name`: the name itself when it reads as
a question, else what the idea is; None for an empty name.*

A name with maths that is a question keeps its maths and its case:

``` python
test_eq(words_q(r'Why scale by $1/\sqrt{d_k}$'), r'Say in one or two sentences: Why scale by $1/\sqrt{d_k}$?')
```

A name that ends with a question mark stays as it is. A plain noun
phrase goes in quotes, with its case. A question word alone is a plain
name, and an empty name gives no question:

``` python
test_eq(words_q('How does attention work?'), 'Say in one or two sentences: How does attention work?')
test_eq(words_q('Bayes?'), 'Say in one or two sentences: Bayes?')
test_eq(words_q('CAN bus'), 'Say in one or two sentences: what is "CAN bus"?')
test_eq(words_q('WHO growth charts'), 'Say in one or two sentences: what is "WHO growth charts"?')
test_eq(words_q('When'), 'Say in one or two sentences: what is "When"?')
test_eq(words_q('whenever'), 'Say in one or two sentences: what is "whenever"?')
test_eq(words_q(''), None); test_eq(words_ask('  '), None)
```


*A choice question on concept `slug` from one model call (and one more
when its words are not plain,
[`plainly`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#plainly)),
or a words question when the call fails (None when the idea has no
name).*

A choice question whose words are hard to read is written again in plain
English, in one more call:

``` python
lrq = temp_learning(); sq = lrq.put('Noise schedule', 'The schedule says how much noise each step adds.', 'ml').slug
hard = 'Which option leverages the schedule; which one is fixed?'
fk = Fake({'Write these texts again': {'q': 'Which part is fixed before training?'}, 'Idea:': dict(q=hard, options=['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'], answer=0)})
test_eq((ask_from_check(lrq, fk, sq)['q'], len(fk.calls)), ('Which part is fixed before training?', 2))
```

### Minutes

A slide with a question takes the minutes of its walk step plus
`talks.ask_min`. The talk takes the sum of its slides, except the parked
slides
([`parked`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#parked)).

### A talk from a walk

Each walk step that is not skipped gives one `idea` slide. A demo or an
order check takes its question from the first gate of the demo that can
be a room question. A step with no demo, or with no such gate, uses its
passage and a short check. A code check gives a words question, because
a talk never runs code. A passage with a small code cell that prints a
value gives a `run` question: “What does this print?” with the code. The
room answers before the presenter runs the cell. With “No code”, a slide
has no demo and no question on code.

[`print_cell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#print_cell)
finds that code cell in the passage. A small cell has at most `RUN_MOST`
simple statements. It prints a value when it calls `print`, or when its
last statement is a value. A cell that draws a picture does not count.
[`print_cell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#print_cell)
gives the cell as one line of code.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L1554"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### print_cell

``` python
def print_cell(
    text:str
)->str | None:
```

*The first small code cell in the markdown `text` that prints a value,
as one line of code, or None.*

A cell that prints, or that ends with a value, counts. An import, a cell
that draws, a loop and a long cell do not count.

``` python
test_eq(print_cell('Add two numbers.\n\n```python\nx = 2\nprint(x + 3)\n```'), 'x = 2; print(x + 3)')
test_eq(print_cell('```python\nimport torch\n```\n\n```python\nxs = [1, 2]\nlen(xs)\n```'), 'xs = [1, 2]; len(xs)')
test_eq([print_cell(f'```python\n{c}\n```') for c in ('import torch', 'show_images(xs)', 'for i in range(3):\n    print(i)', 'a = 1\nb = 2\nc = 3\nprint(a)')], [None] * 4)
print_cell('```python\nprint(2 + 3)\n```')
```

[`code_piece`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#code_piece)
gives the one short piece of code that a notebook slide shows: the first
small code cell of the section, with no blank lines. A cell of imports
only, a cell that draws and a long cell do not count. A cell with a line
longer than `cols` characters does not count either: the room cannot
scroll, and at the least size of slide code such a line passes the right
edge of the slide. A slide whose code is beside its points, a figure or
a demo has room for `CODE_COLS` characters, and code alone has room for
`CODE_COLS_ALONE`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L1567"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### code_piece

``` python
def code_piece(
    text:str, cols:int=50
)->str:
```

*The first small code cell in the markdown `text` (at most `CODE_LINES`
lines of at most `cols` characters, not imports only, no picture), as a
\`\`\`python block, or ’’.*

The import cell does not count, so the piece is the next cell, with its
blank line gone. A long cell gives no piece. A cell with a line that is
too long for the slide gives no piece, so the next cell is the piece.

``` python
test_eq(code_piece('Setup.\n\n```python\nimport os\n```\n\nRun it.\n\n```python\nx = 2\n\nprint(x + 3)\n```'), '```python\nx = 2\nprint(x + 3)\n```')
test_eq(code_piece('```python\n' + '\n'.join(f'a{i} = {i}' for i in range(9)) + '\n```'), '')
test_eq(code_piece('No code here.'), '')
wide = '```python\nx = ' + 'a' * 70 + '\nprint(x)\n```\n\n```python\ny = 1\nprint(y)\n```'
test_eq(code_piece(wide), '```python\ny = 1\nprint(y)\n```')
test_eq(code_piece(wide, CODE_COLS_ALONE), '```python\nx = ' + 'a' * 70 + '\nprint(x)\n```')
```

[`_idea_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#_idea_ask)
gives the demo slug (or None) and the question of one step.

[`_idea`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#_idea)
makes the slide of one step. Its beats show the passage, then the
figure, then the demo, each when the slide has it. The slide keeps the
source of its passage, so the editor, the room and the recap file can
name it. A section of a notebook (a step whose passage has `cells`) is
not a slide as it is: its headings, code and tables are too much for a
room. So the whole section goes to the slide writer in
[`_read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#_read), and
the slide shows only the short piece of
[`code_piece`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#code_piece)
(none with “No code”), the points that the writer makes from the
section, and the question. The run question still comes from the whole
section. With “No code”, another passage that has code does not show
either. The slide writer gets it in
[`_read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#_read) and
says in words what the code does.
[`_unread`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#_unread)
takes [`_read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#_read)
away before the talk is saved.

### What the slides say

A walk from a paper or a link gives each slide a passage. A walk from a
topic does not: its steps have no passage, and the tutor note of a step
comes only when a learner opens the step. So the tutor writes the
content of each slide when the talk is made. A slide with no passage
gets 2 to 4 points for the room. Each slide with no speaker note gets
one: what to say, one question to ask the room, and one common confusion
to watch for. A slide with a passage keeps it, and gets only the notes.

The prompt `talk.slide` asks for both, with one model call for each
slide. You can change it on the Settings page.

[`_body`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#_body) gives
the reply as points and notes, or None when it is bad.
[`slide_notes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#slide_notes)
writes the notes as Markdown.
