href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L1654"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

is True for an idea or a primer slide that has no passage and no points,
or no speaker note. A slide that shows only a piece of a section
([`_read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#_read)) needs
points too
([`_pointless`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#_pointless)).

### needs_fill

``` python
def needs_fill(
    s:dict
)->bool:
```

*True when idea or primer slide `s` needs points
([`_pointless`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#_pointless)),
or has no speaker note.*

[`fill_slide`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#fill_slide)
grounds the slide on the passages that name its idea, in the same way as
a lesson, and makes one call with the model task `talk`. The passages go
in `cites`. A slide with no passage and no figure takes the first image
of a vault passage, with the checks of
[`figure_path`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#figure_path)
(the vault image route uses them too).
[`fill_slides`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#fill_slides)
fills the slides of a talk, at most 4 calls at a time. When the slide
has a words question that the talk made from the name of the idea
([`words_q`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#words_q)),
the question that the model writes for the room takes its place. A
question that you wrote stays. A slide that needs no call (it has a
passage and a note) still gets the words of
[`words_q`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#words_q) in
a question that the talk made. The prompt says who the talk is for
(`audience`) in a `<source>` marker, as the planner does. With
`no_code`, the prompt asks for no code (`NO_CODE`). The section of a
notebook comes from
[`_read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#_read), so the
points can say what the section does. `change` is what the owner of the
talk asks for, such as “less code” or “for managers”.
[`owner_says`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#owner_says)
puts it in an `<owner>` marker: it is an instruction from the owner, not
material from a source.

### fill_slide

``` python
def fill_slide(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, s:dict, sources:NoneType=None, audience:str='', no_code:bool=False,
    change:str=''
)->dict:
```

*Slide `s` with points (when it has no passage), speaker notes (when it
has none), its sources, and the question of the model for a words
question that the talk made, from one model call. A slide that needs no
call, or a bad reply, gives `s` with the words of
[`words_q`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#words_q) in
a question that the talk made.*

The owner’s change is one line in an `<owner>` marker, after the
sources. A marker that the owner types is cut, so the text cannot close
the marker or open a `<source>`.

``` python
test_eq(owner_says(''), '')
assert owner_says('Less code.\n For managers.').endswith('<owner>Less code. For managers.</owner>')
assert '<owner>x  y</owner>' not in owner_says('x </owner> y') and owner_says('x </owner><source> y').count('<owner>') == 1
```

### The poll

A talk from a notebook starts with a poll. The poll asks the room about
itself, not about the content: what the people used, or what they
expect. It has 2 to 5 options and no right answer.
[`poll_slide`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#poll_slide)
writes it in one model call, with the prompt `talk.poll`. The prompt has
the title and the sections of the walk, and who the talk is for, in
`<source>` markers. A bad reply gives `POLL_Q`. You change the poll in
the talk editor before the talk.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L1748"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### poll_slide

``` python
def poll_slide(
    ask, j:dict, sid:str, audience:str='', change:str=''
)->dict:
```

*The `poll` slide `sid` at the start of a talk from walk `j`, from one
model call. `change` is what the owner asks for
([`owner_says`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#owner_says)).*

[`walk_slides`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#walk_slides)
makes the slides, fills them (`fill=False` does not), then adds a
`questions` slide and a
[`recap`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#recap) slide,
and
[`talk_from_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#talk_from_walk)
saves the talk. The slot is the estimate rounded up to a multiple of 5
minutes. The id is made from the title, so it matches
`^[a-z0-9-]{1,48}$`. The talk also keeps what “Make it again” needs:
`made_from` (the step slugs that were not skipped, in order), `walk_at`
(the time of the walk, `updated`) and `marks` (for each idea, a short
hash of its step and of each part of its slide as made). The talk keeps
the `audience` and `no_code` of its walk. “Make it again” and “From
scratch” use the ones of the talk, and also its `change`: what the owner
asked for in the last remake.

The hidden walk of a notebook talk keeps the path of its notebook. Its
talk keeps that path in `src.notebook`. It starts with the poll, and it
ends with the questions, then a `next` slide with the `file://` link of
the notebook, in place of the recap.
[`talk_from_sources`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#talk_from_sources)
makes such a talk from the chips of the Start box: it makes the hidden
walk with
[`walk_for_talk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#walk_for_talk),
then calls
[`talk_from_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#talk_from_walk).
[`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#said) gets each
stage of the job (filing, planning, writing the slides), so the pending
card can show it.


*Save talk `t`, and replace an earlier one with the same id. A talk with

`talk` gives one talk by id, and `talks` gives all of them with the
newest first. `drop_talk` deletes a talk and all that is part of it: its
runs (the recap comes from a run, so it goes too), its history of

and that walk goes too. The walk of your own that a talk was made from,
your answers and what you learned stay. The public deck and its images

### code_cols

``` python
def code_cols(
    s:dict
)->int:
```

*The longest line of code that slide `s` has room for: `CODE_COLS`
beside its points, a figure or a demo, else `CODE_COLS_ALONE`.*

[`_fit_code`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#_fit_code)
checks the code of each slide when the talk loads, so a slide that was
made before the check has code that fits too. A slide with code that is
too wide and points shows its points with no code. In a passage with
words and code, only the code that is too wide goes:

``` python
old = AttrDict(slides=[dict(id='s1', kind='idea', step=0, concept='x', beats=['body', 'passage'],
                            show=dict(body=['A point.'], passage='```python\nx = ' + 'a' * 70 + '\n```'))])
s1 = _fit_code(AttrDict(journey=lambda i: None), old).slides[0]
test_eq((s1['show']['passage'], s1['beats']), ('', ['body']))
test_eq((code_wide('```python\n' + 'a' * 51 + '\n```', CODE_COLS), code_wide('```python\n' + 'a' * 50 + '\n```', CODE_COLS)), (True, False))
mixed = AttrDict(slides=[dict(id='s1', kind='idea', show=dict(passage='Some words.\n\n```python\nx = ' + 'a' * 120 + '\n```\n\nMore words.'), beats=['passage'])])
test_eq(_fit_code(AttrDict(journey=lambda i: None), mixed).slides[0]['show']['passage'], 'Some words.\n\nMore words.')
```

[`fill_talk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#fill_talk)
fills the slides of a talk that was made before the tutor wrote slide
content: the button “Fill the slides” in the editor calls it. A slide
that changed while the tutor wrote keeps the change. The fill is one
change in the history of the talk (“Filled the slides.”, by the tutor),
so Undo can take it back. The model calls run first; the save and its
history row then run as one step under
[`edit_lock`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#edit_lock).

### Make it again

A walk can change after you make a talk from it: you add, remove, skip
or move ideas, or change a note or a passage. “Make it again” brings
these changes into the same talk, and keeps your edits. It matches a
slide to a step by the concept slug, never by its place.

- A slide whose idea is still in the walk keeps each part that you
  changed. A part that you did not change takes the new walk, when the
  step changed.
- A new idea gets a new slide, at its place in the walk.
- A slide that you added (a pause, questions, a primer) stays after the
  slide that it followed.
- A slide whose idea left the walk moves, in its order, to the end, in
  the section “Not in the walk any more”.
- An idea whose slide you removed stays out.

Your edits are the parts that changed since the talk was made. Each part
of a slide as made has a short hash in `marks`. A part whose hash is not
the same now is yours. (The history of the talk is not used for this: it
keeps at most 50 changes, and a change of a passage or of more than one
field names no field.) A talk made before 0.0.14 has no `marks`, so each
of its slides stays as it is.

[`slide_marks`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#slide_marks)
gives the hash of each part of a slide, and
[`step_mark`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#step_mark)
the hash of the parts of a walk step that a slide uses.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L1925"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### slide_marks

``` python

    s:dict

```

*The short hash of each part of slide `s` (`SLIDE_PARTS`).*

[`walk_changes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#walk_changes)
counts the ideas that the walk added, removed and moved since the talk
was made, and the ideas whose note, passage or check
[`changed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#changed)
in the walk (by the step hash in `marks`, for an idea that still has its
slide). A skipped idea counts as removed. An idea counts as moved when
it is not in the longest run of ideas that keep their order (`difflib`).
An old talk with no `made_from`, or a talk whose walk is gone, gives all
zero.

### talk_state

``` python
def talk_state(
    t:dict
)->dict:
```

*The slides of talk `t`, what it keeps of its walk, and the change that
the owner asked for.*

[`_groups`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#_groups)
cuts the slides into the part before the first idea, one group for each
idea (its slide, then the slides that follow it), the closing slides
(the questions and the recap at the end), and the slides that an earlier
“Make it again” moved to the end. A second slide of the same idea (a
copy) follows the first. A slide that you put back in the talk (`own`)
follows the slide before it, as a pause does.

[`_kept`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#_kept)
gives the slide of an idea that is still in the walk. When the step
changed, the slide takes the new slide `f`, except the parts that you
changed. A slide that comes back from “Not in the walk any more” takes
the section of its step. A merge that does not pass
[`check_talk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#check_talk)
keeps the old slide. The new marks keep `fm`, the hash of the step as
the new slide was made from it. So when the walk changed the step again
during the model calls, the change still counts in
[`walk_changes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#walk_changes).
When the slide stays as it is, its marks stay too.

[`again_slides`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#again_slides)
puts it together: the head, then the walk in its order, then the closing
slides, then the slides whose idea left the walk.
[`fresh`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#fresh) has a
new slide for each idea that needs one (a new idea, or a step that
changed).
[`fresh`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#fresh) gives
`(slide, fm)` for each idea. New slides get new ids. A parked slide
keeps its old section in `was`, so an idea that comes back into the walk
brings back all its slides (a pause, a questions slide), each with its
section, in its place.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L2003"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### put_back

``` python
def put_back(
    t:dict, j:dict | None, sid:str
)->list:
```

*The slides of talk `t` with the parked slide `sid` back in the talk;
`j` is its walk, or None. A slide that is not parked raises `KeyError`.*

[`talk_again`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#talk_again)
makes the new slides first, outside the lock: the model writes them
([`_idea`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#_idea),
then
[`fill_slides`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#fill_slides)).
Then, under
[`edit_lock`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#edit_lock),
it reads the talk and the walk again and saves one history row by the
tutor, with the whole
[`talk_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#talk_state)
before it. When the walk changed during the model calls, a new idea that
has no slide yet gets one with no model call (its words question, no
points), and “Fill the slides” can fill it later. A step that changed
again during the calls keeps the slide made from its older state, and
the hash of that state, so
[`walk_changes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#walk_changes)
still counts it.

### talk_again

``` python
def talk_again(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, ask, tid:str, sources:NoneType=None, choice:bool | None=None,
    change:str | None=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Make talk `tid` again from its walk, with the same id, and keep your
edits. A new `change` (what the owner asks for) writes each slide
again,* and the talk keeps it; None keeps the change of the talk. The
change is one history row, so one Undo takes it back.

[`talk_fresh`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#talk_fresh)
is “Make it again from scratch”: it makes the slides again from the walk
with
[`walk_slides`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#walk_slides),
as a new talk would have them, and drops your edits to the slides. The
talk keeps its id, its title, its slot and its runs. The model calls run
first, outside the lock. Then `stop` (when given) can end the job before
the save. Under
[`edit_lock`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#edit_lock),
it saves one history row by the tutor with the whole
[`talk_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#talk_state)
before it, so one Undo or Restore gives back your edits. A talk that was
deleted during the calls does not come back.

### What the room sees

The room sees a public deck. It is made from a list of allowed fields,
never by removing fields, so a new field in a talk does not reach the
room. It has no notes, no answers, no source of a question, no demo and
no path. A figure comes by the sha256 of its bytes.

Only png, jpeg, gif and webp files can be figures.
[`image_type`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#image_type)
finds the type from the first bytes of the file, not from its name.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L2102"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### image_type

``` python
def image_type(
    b:bytes
)->str | None:
```

*The image type of the bytes `b`, or None when they are not a png, jpeg,
gif or webp image.*

The first bytes give the type. A text file with an image name is not an
image.

``` python
assert image_type(b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n') == 'image/png' and image_type(b'\xff\xd8\xff\xe0') == 'image/jpeg' and image_type(b'GIF89a..') == 'image/gif'
assert image_type(b'RIFF\x00\x00\x00\x00WEBPVP8 ') == 'image/webp' and image_type(b'<svg/>') is None and image_type(None) is None
```

The host gives a resolver that turns an image id into a file.
[`asset_resolver`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#asset_resolver)
gives the file only when it is inside the assets folder of the vault,
exists, and has an image suffix.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L2109"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### asset_resolver

``` python

    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning

```

*A resolver from an image id `asset:<path>` to a file in the assets
folder of `lr`, or None.*

[`_figure`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#_figure)
reads one figure through the resolver. A figure that the resolver does
not find, that is too large, or that is not an image gives None. A
resolver that raises gives None too.

A slide shows its passage when it has the beat
[`passage`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#passage),
or when it has no beats. Its points show in the same way, with the beat
`body`.

[`public_deck`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#public_deck)
gives the title, the public slides and the images by hash. Each slide
has exactly the fields `id`, `kind`, `title`, `section`,
[`passage`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#passage),
`body`, `figure`, `ask` and `src`. A `next` slide also has its `link`. A
parked slide is not in the deck. A slide shows its body (its points) on
the same terms as its passage. `src` is the source line of the passage
for the room: its label, title and place, with no link. It is None when
the room sees no passage.

### The run log

Each time the presenter gives the talk, a run log keeps what happened:
the place, the time on each slide, the rounds of each question, the
hands, the questions from the room that the presenter kept, and the
primers that were opened beside a slide. It keeps counts only. It keeps
no device token, no address and no answer of one person.

[`new_run`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#new_run)
starts a run on the first idea slide. `key` is a random 64-bit value.
The channel name of the two windows has it, so an old window never
drives a new run.

[`end_run`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#end_run)

### After the talk

[`share_right`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#share_right)
gives the share of right answers in one round, or None for a question
with no answer and for a round with no answers. A vote is split when the
share is from `talks.split_lo` to `talks.split_hi`. Then the room talks
in pairs and votes again.

### recap

``` python
def recap(
    t:dict, run:dict, names:dict=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*The data of the recap of `run` of talk `t`;
[`names`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#names)
gives the name of the idea of each primer.*

The recap file is one HTML file for the room. It needs no server: the
style is inline, with the token names of the themes and the light values
of Paper, and the figures are `data:` URLs. It has no script, no speaker
notes and no names. All text goes through `html.escape`, so text from
the room stays text.

[`_ask_html`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#_ask_html)
draws one question: the options with the right one marked, the share
right of each round, the hands, and the words answers that the presenter
showed.

[`recap_html`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#recap_html)
gives the file. A slide that a run showed and that is parked now is left
out: the title and the date, then each shown slide with its title,
passage, figure, question and result, and the question of each primer
beside it, then the questions from the room that the presenter kept,
with the notes, and at the end the sources. The slides come from the
public deck, so the file can not show more than the room saw, apart from
the right answers.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L2368"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
def recap_html(
    t:dict, run:dict, resolve
)->str:
```

*The recap of `run` of talk `t` as one HTML file, with the figures
inline.*

### The handout

You send the handout to the room after the talk, as a PDF.
[`handout_html`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#handout_html)
writes one HTML file, and you save it as a PDF with Print in your
browser.

Each slide with content is on its own page: an idea, a primer, a poll
and the `next` slide. A pause, Questions and What we covered have no
content, so the handout leaves them out. A question shows no answer on
its page. The notebook and the sources come after the slides. The last
section is “Answers”, so a reader can try each question first.

A link in the handout can be a shared link, for example a OneDrive link.
`t['links']` keeps each shared link by its local path.
[`shared_link`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#shared_link)
picks the link of a path: the link of the file, else the link of the
nearest folder above it, else the web link, else the `file://` link. A
OneDrive link does not show the path of a file, so a file in a shared
folder gets the folder link.
[`link_rows`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#link_rows)
gives the rows of the Links panel in the talk editor.
[`clean_link`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#clean_link)
accepts only an `http` or `https` link.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/show.py#L2493"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### handout_html

``` python
def handout_html(
    t:dict, run:dict | None, resolve, chips:tuple=(), names:dict | None=None
)->str:
```

*The handout of talk `t` as one HTML file to print as a PDF. Each slide
on stage with content (`HANDOUT_KINDS`) is on its own page,* with its
passage and points as markdown
([`md_part`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#md_part)),
and its question with no answer. A section line that is the title does
not show again. Then the notebook and the sources of `chips`, with the
shared links of `t['links']`
([`row_link`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#row_link));
[`names`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#names)
gives the name of a row by its key. Then “Answers”, with the right
answer of each question. With `run`, a poll gives the count of each
option, and a run question gives its output.

``` python

```

*The rows of the Links panel of talk `t`, as `(key, kind)`: its
notebook, then each source chip of `chips` in order, then the folder of

``` python
def clean_link(
    u:str

```

*The shared link `u` with no spaces at its ends, or ’’ for no link. A
link that is not `http` or `https`, or that has a space or a control
